head: claude/alpaca-ext-hours-close-qty
title: alpaca: name the broker-side cancel wedge both close paths could not distinguish
body:
## What this is

Tier-2, **ORDER PATH** (`AlpacaClient.close` / `_close_extended_hours`). Opened as a **DRAFT for operator approval — do not merge on my account.**

Dispatched on the live `alpaca_paper` GLD *"Position CLOSE failing — won't flatten"* pages.

---

## ⚠️ The briefed diagnosis is refuted — and that is half the finding

I was told this was an uncovered sibling call site: `BL-20260708-ALPACA-CLOSE-QTY-AVAILABLE` was fixed for the regular-hours loop and `_close_extended_hours` never got it. **Verified against the code and the live fleet, that does not hold.**

| Claim | What I measured |
|---|---|
| The ext-hours path never got the `qty_available` fix | **PR #10666 already ported it**, merged `2026-09-01T16:23Z` — ~4h *before* the 20:12Z measurement in my brief |
| The fix isn't deployed | **It is deployed and running.** Its new self-diagnosing log line `alpaca extended-hours close GLD still insufficient-qty after ~6.0s` was firing on the trader at 21:19Z |
| It's extended-hours-specific | **The regular-hours path fails identically** at 13:30–13:34Z the same day — inside RTH — and that path already has *both* `_await_qty_available` **and** the `DELETE /v2/positions/{sym}?cancel_orders=true` escalation |

So there was **no working sibling to port from**. Porting would have fixed nothing.

## Actual cause: a broker-side wedge

```
GLD OCO parent 2e843e04-5487-470c-a702-70e796fbd05e
  status:      "pending_cancel"
  canceled_at: null
  submitted_at: 2026-08-27T14:11:32Z     <- five days
  qty: 39   filled_qty: 0
```

Those 39 shares stay `held_for_orders`, so `qty_available: 0` on **every** path. Our `DELETE` **was accepted** — that is what moved the order to `pending_cancel` — and Alpaca then never completed its own cancel, so a re-issued app-level cancel is a no-op and `cancel_orders=true` returns the same `insufficient qty available for order (requested: 39, available: 0)`.

That is **`BL-20260716-ALPACA-QQQ-WEDGED-PENDING-CANCEL` recurring**. The existing code comment already concedes this is past the last programmatic lever.

**Scope question answered:** the ask was *"make the extended-hours path release the reserved qty the same way the regular close does, **or establish that it cannot and say why**."* It is the second branch, definitively — the regular path does not do it differently, and its one extra lever (`cancel_orders=true`) is a **market liquidation that cannot fill outside RTH** and is *already failing in RTH anyway*. There is nothing to port.

---

## What this PR actually changes

Two things that **are** defective in our code, both provable:

### 1. Nothing read the field that distinguishes the two cases

The residual order dict already carried `status`. Both give-up paths logged the whole dict and **neither ever branched on it** — so a transient cancel race (a retry clears it) and a permanent broker wedge (no retry *ever* clears it) produced a byte-identical `retMsg`, ERROR and page, every tick, indefinitely. The operator could not tell *"wait"* from *"this needs venue action."*

New pure `classify_share_hold()` → four **never-collapsed** states:

- `residual_unreadable` — *we could not look* (emphatically **not** `no_residual_orders`)
- `no_residual_orders`
- `broker_cancel_wedged` — **the finding**
- `orders_still_resting` — a retry may well work

Both paths now carry it in the log **and** the `retMsg`. Live-shaped output:

```
extended-hours limit close rejected: insufficient qty available for order
(requested: 39, available: 0) [share_hold=broker_cancel_wedged: 1 order(s)
wedged broker-side (2e843e04-... is pending_cancel) — the cancel was ACCEPTED
and Alpaca never completed it, so no further app-level cancel or
cancel_orders=true liquidation can release these shares; this needs
operator/venue action]
```

### 2. The cancel helper threw the broker's answer away

`_request` **"never raises on HTTP"** (its own docstring), so `_cancel_open_orders_for_symbol`'s `except Exception` was **dead code for every broker rejection**. It returned cancels **ISSUED**, not **ACCEPTED** — which `close()`'s `if n_cancelled` settle-wait gate keyed on — and collapsed a **failed** open-orders read (`None`) into *"nothing to cancel"* (`[]`).

Same shape as `BL-20260825-PLACE-PROTECTIVE-COUNTS-THE-CANCEL-CALL-NOT-ITS-EFFECT`, one venue over. `_cancel_open_orders_detailed` now reports `accepted / already_gone / refused / could_not_look` and logs refusals with the broker's reason. The wrapper keeps its `int` contract but returns **accepted**.

### 3. `operator_alerts` diag allowlist entry (Tier-1, read-only)

See the alarm section below.

---

## ⚠️ What this does NOT do

**It does not close the wedged GLD position.** No bot-side lever releases an Alpaca `pending_cancel` — that needs operator/venue action. I am not claiming otherwise.

The close deliberately **still returns `retCode 1`** (a real failure), never a defer, because the failure this subsystem exists to end is the *silent retry loop*. A test asserts the new text contains none of `order_monitor`'s defer trigger phrases (`exit deferred` / `deferring` / `market closed`) — that string-match is how a defer is detected, so a stray phrase would book a real failure as "venue merely shut".

---

## The two things I was asked to weigh

### (1) Is `alpaca_live` exposed? — **Structurally yes; not realised.**

`alpaca_live` is `mode: live`, `account_class: real_money`, shares this exact client code, and **trades GLD** (its roster overlaps `alpaca_paper` on 11 symbols). So the same wedge would strand a real-money equity position identically on both paths.

Measured `2026-09-01T21:23Z`: `alpaca_live` is **flat — zero positions, zero resting orders** (`/api/diag/exchange_positions`, `/api/diag/alpaca_open_orders`). **No real money is stranded right now.** The exposure is the next real-money equity close that meets a wedged order.

### (2) Does this page the operator repeatedly? — **I could not measure it, and that is itself a finding.**

#10666's exponential backoff (300s floor, doubling, hourly clamp, never silent) **is** deployed. But I cannot show it works:

- `/api/bot/notifications` renders only the **current** banner — no history, no rate.
- The page ring `runtime_logs/operator_alerts.jsonl` was **not** on the diag `log_file` allowlist → HTTP 400, unreadable from a relay-bound session.
- ⚠️ **The obvious substitute is a trap, and I nearly fell in it.** These alerts do **not** ride `outcomes.jsonl`, so `/api/bot/logs?level=error,warn` shows **zero** close-failure rows. Measured over the full 1000-row ERROR/WARN feed (`2026-08-21T23:36Z → 2026-09-01T20:47Z`): zero — *while the banner was rendering an active `close_failure` for GLD at that moment.* A reviewer grading alarm health from the documented ERROR feed would conclude this alarm has never fired in eleven days.

This PR adds the allowlist entry so the rate becomes measurable. **Grading the backoff still needs a live read after this deploys** — I am reporting it as unmeasured, not as fine.

*Separately noted, not fixed here:* 839 of those 1000 ERROR/WARN rows (**83.9%**) are `strategy_builder` no-candle exceptions across six legs — the alarm-fatigue condition `BL-20260825-TRANSIENT-CLASSIFIER-MISSES-THE-VARIANT-FAMILIES` already owns. Still live, and worse than when filed.

---

## Verification

- **11 new tests**, executed directly (**pytest is absent from this sandbox**) — **all pass**, including one replaying the exact live residual (`2e843e04` `pending_cancel` + its `held` OCO child, which must *not* by itself grade as a wedge) and one asserting no defer phrase leaks.
- End-to-end run of `_close_extended_hours` against the live residual shape: `retCode 1` preserved, broker text preserved, wedge named.
- `ruff check` — clean.
- `run_guards.py` — only `artifact-validity-guard` and `operator-owed-guard` fail, **both solely** because `python3 -m pytest` is unavailable here (confirmed by running it directly). Per the dispatch brief these are tooling, not defects.
- Backlog appended via `scripts/ops/backlog_append.py` with `similar_ok=True` (RECURRENCEs, candidates read): **18 insertions / 0 deletions** — no reformat.

**Deliberately NOT registered with `collapsed-state-guard`:** no consumer *branches* on the four states yet (they are formatted into a message). Registering today would either fail the guard or invite the decorative branch it exists to prevent — the same reasoning CLAUDE.md applies to `BYBIT_HEDGE_MODE_SYMBOLS`.

## Backlog rows filed

- `BL-20260901-ALPACA-CANCEL-WEDGE-UNNAMED` (high) — the recurrence, both halves
- `BL-20260901-OPERATOR-ALERTS-HAS-NO-READ-SURFACE` (medium) — 4th instance of the no-read-surface shape

## Operator decision requested

1. Approve the Tier-2 order-path change (points 1–2 above).
2. **The live GLD wedge needs your action** — an Alpaca paper-console reset or venue-side cancel of `2e843e04`. Nothing in this PR clears it.
3. Worth deciding: should a confirmed `broker_cancel_wedged` keep paging at full close-failure severity forever, or escalate to a distinct *"needs venue action"* alert? Today it rides the ordinary page, which is the desensitisation risk.
